The mode also scans the Azure OpenAI "On Your Data" per-data-source instruction at `data_sources[].parameters.role_information` (and the original extensions-API camelCase `dataSources[].parameters.roleInformation`), which the backend applies as a de-facto system prompt — so a payload smuggled there cannot bypass content scanning.

Detection and redaction cover exactly the same set of fields: every field the Content-mode detector walks, `action: redact` rewrites. An asymmetry would be a fail-open bypass — the PII reported as removed while the provider receives the original value. For request bodies that carry prompt text in other, non-standard fields, use `scan_fields: "all"`.

**`exclude_roles` is a content-mode control.** In `scan_fields: "content"` it suppresses the listed message roles as described above. In `scan_fields: "all"` it does not apply at all: that mode's contract is to scan the entire request body, so its detector and recursive redactor walk every value regardless of role and a configured `exclude_roles: [system]` does not preserve a system message there. Use `scan_fields: "content"` when role exemptions must hold.

In `scan_fields: "all"` mode, detection and redaction use the same top-level exception. Scalar strings or numbers under structural keys (`model`, `id`, `role`, `type`, etc.) and numeric values under tuning keys (`temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, `seed`, etc.) are control parameters and do not trigger policy. String values under numeric tuning keys remain scannable. The walker always recurses into nested objects and arrays and never exempts nested occurrences of those names, so PII hidden under a structural key (e.g. `{"metadata": {"type": "<PII>"}}` or `{"id": {"note": "<PII>"}}`) is still detected and redacted. When the body has a recognized chat shape (`messages` array), the structured redactor that touches `messages[].content` runs first and the recursive walker then covers sibling fields. Raw contextual custom patterns remain enforceable when they span structural JSON outside an exempt scalar.

Bodies above `max_scan_bytes` never silently bypass enforcing policy: `reject` and `redact` return `413`, while `warn` continues with an `ai_shield_warnings=body_too_large` event.

**MCP tool arguments (`scan_fields: "mcp_arguments"`).** For an agent-facing MCP endpoint, neither of the other modes fits: `content` looks for LLM prompt fields a JSON-RPC envelope never has, and `all` also scans the envelope itself (`jsonrpc`, `method`, `params.name`, ids). `mcp_arguments` scans exactly the tool input: the `params.arguments` of every JSON-RPC `tools/call` request — a singleton, or each `tools/call` member of a batch — and nothing else. Other methods (`initialize`, `tools/list`, notifications, …) carry no arguments and pass unscanned.

- **Detection** walks every decoded string value, object key, and number under `params.arguments` (the text the tool receives, after JSON escapes are resolved) and additionally runs the patterns over the arguments' compact serialization, so a contextual `custom_pattern` spanning a key and its value (`"password"\s*:`) still matches. No structural exemption applies: every argument is caller-supplied tool input.
- **Media types** match `mcp_gateway`'s admission: `application/json`, `application/json-rpc`, any `+json`, or a `POST` with no `Content-Type`, so omitting the header cannot carry a tool call past the shield. For `+json` gRPC-Web media types, this applies only to bare JSON bodies; `mcp_gateway` refuses framed payloads, which pass the shield uninspected unless they look like JSON that may carry a call (**Unparseable bodies**).
- **Duplicate member names** make it parser-dependent which `arguments` a server executes, so `reject` and `redact` refuse such a body with `400` (`ai_shield_rejected=ambiguous_json`) and `warn` records `ai_shield_warnings=ambiguous_json`. (`mcp_gateway` refuses the same body with `-32600`.)
- **Unparseable bodies.** A body the whole-document JSON parse refuses passes uninspected only when it is not recognizable as a JSON document that could carry a `tools/call` — an empty bridged body, a REST body, base64 `grpc-web-text`, or malformed JSON that names no call: it carries no byte-order mark, no NUL byte ahead of a JSON-shaped lead character (`{`, `[`, `/`, `#`), its first byte after ASCII whitespace (including JSON5's `\v` and `\f`) is not `/`, `#`, or non-ASCII, and it either does not open with `{` or `[` or contains neither the literal `tools/call` nor a JSON escape. That is a recognizability test, not a proof that no reader anywhere could find a call. Anything else may still execute: `mcp_gateway` admits batch members one at a time, each with its own parser recursion budget, so a batch can exceed the whole-document nesting limit while every member is still admitted and executed, and a lenient upstream decoder (Python's `json`, JSON5) accepts a byte-order mark, UTF-16 / UTF-32, `NaN`, `Infinity`, comments, JSON5 whitespace (no-break space, U+2028, form feed), or trailing commas that the shield's parser refuses. Such a body — and any non-UTF-8 body — is refused with `400` by `reject` and `redact` (`ai_shield_rejected=jsonrpc_request_unparseable`); `warn` records `ai_shield_warnings=jsonrpc_request_unparseable` and forwards it. `before_proxy` and the final-body re-check make the same decision for the same bytes; a non-UTF-8 body is first seen by the final re-check, because the proxy gives `before_proxy` no UTF-8 view of it. A legitimate OpenAPI bridge call is unaffected: its final body is empty or valid JSON. Because malformed or encoded JSON bodies that may carry a call are refused, scope `scan_fields: mcp_arguments` to MCP routes only. The same applies to `ai_transcript_audit`: with `capture.mcp_tool_calls` on, an unparseable body the same test flags is staged as an MCP audit candidate, so it counts against the plugin's staging permits and retained-byte budget. Only JSON-shaped bodies are flagged for NUL bytes (UTF-16 / UTF-32 JSON whose first character opens a value or comment), so a binary upload such as a PNG or JPEG is not.
- **Request charset.** The shield reads the body as UTF-8, so an in-scope request whose `Content-Type` declares any other `charset` is refused with `400` (`ai_shield_rejected=unsupported_charset`) by `reject` and `redact` before the body is parsed, and `warn` records `ai_shield_warnings=unsupported_charset` and forwards it without scanning. `utf-8` and `utf8` are accepted case-insensitively, quoted or not, with whitespace around `;` and `=`; no `charset` at all is accepted. Any RFC 2231 form (`charset*`, `charset*0`, ...) is refused whatever its value, because some parsers (Go's `mime`, Werkzeug) decode it and let it override a plain `charset`. UTF-7 is the motivating case: it is plain ASCII and parses as JSON, so the shield would scan the encoded text while an upstream that decodes by charset executes the real arguments. The final-body re-check applies the same rule to the final `Content-Type`. `mcp_gateway` refuses the same requests with JSON-RPC `-32600` before routing.
- **Redaction** rewrites argument values in place and re-detects over the rewritten arguments; PII that a value rewrite cannot remove (an object key, a cross-token contextual match) fails the request closed with `400`, exactly as in `all` mode. `mcp_gateway` admits the redacted arguments: an upstream MCP tool receives them redacted, and through the OpenAPI bridge redacted query, header, and body arguments are forwarded redacted in the rebuilt REST request after the gateway re-validates the same tool and JSON-RPC id against the admitted schema. A redacted **path** argument is not forwarded: a placeholder such as `[REDACTED:email]` is not a canonical path segment, so the bridged call fails with JSON-RPC `-32602` (`Invalid MCP tool arguments`) and nothing reaches the backend. Keep values that may carry PII out of path parameters, or expect such calls to be refused.
- **JSON-RPC correlation values must round-trip.** If an id or `params._meta.progressToken` cannot be preserved by JSON parsing and serialization (for example `1e3` or a non-canonical large integer), or the recognizer cannot inspect an over-bound request, `redact` refuses the request with `400` and emits no rewritten body. Ids correlate the MCP response, and progress tokens correlate progress notifications.
- **The final request body is re-checked** like every other mode. For an upstream `tools/call` that is the gateway's upstream-named envelope (same arguments); for an OpenAPI bridge call it is the REST body, which is not a `tools/call` and is not re-scanned — its content was built from the arguments the shield already decided, and the gateway refuses any later change to it.
- Rejections use this plugin's ordinary `400` / `413` JSON bodies, not JSON-RPC errors.

**The final backend-visible body is authoritative.** `before_proxy` is not the last word on what a backend receives: every `transform_request_body` hook — a `request_transformer` body rule, a header-to-body overlay, a custom body plugin — runs afterwards and can put policy-relevant content back into the request, and a header rewrite (`request_transformer` relabelling `text/plain` to `application/json`, say) can bring a request into scope that `before_proxy` skipped. `on_final_request_body` therefore decides scope again from the **final** headers and re-decides every in-scope `POST` over the exact dispatched representation, after all request-body transforms. `reject` and `warn` re-decide there normally; `redact` fails the request closed with `400`, because that hook can refuse a request but cannot rewrite wire bytes, so PII still present at dispatch time is an unfulfilled redaction obligation. A rejection there precedes backend dispatch and finalized-request egress. An uninspectable final body gets the same verdict `before_proxy` gives it: a declared-JSON body that is not readable UTF-8 JSON fails closed for enforcing actions, and a sniffed non-JSON body passes.

**Compressed request bodies.** With the co-located `compression` plugin's `decompress_request` enabled, request decoding runs in the shared pre-`before_proxy` normalization phase, so the encoding header is already gone when the shield runs: ordinary compressed requests are scanned — and, in `redact` mode, rewritten and forwarded — like plaintext. For `mcp_arguments`, any in-scope request that still carries a non-identity `Content-Encoding` at `before_proxy` is rejected with `400`, including in `warn` mode, because the bounded MCP recognizer cannot inspect encoded bytes. Other scan modes retain deferred compressed-body behavior: `reject`/`redact` fail closed when no decoder produces plaintext — for a sniffed body too, whatever its `Content-Type` — and `warn` records `ai_shield_warnings=compressed_body` for declared JSON and leaves an encoded sniffed body alone.

```yaml
plugin_name: ai_prompt_shield
config:
  action: redact
  patterns: [ssn, credit_card, email, api_key, aws_key]
  custom_patterns:
    - name: internal_account
      regex: "ACCT-\\d{8}"
  exclude_roles: [system]
```

### `ai_prompt_compressor`

**Priority:** 4055 · **Phases:** `before_proxy`, `transform_request_body_with_context`, `on_final_request_body_with_context` · **Protocols:** HTTP · **Failure policy:** `KeepLastKnownGood`

Shortens prompt text to cut LLM token usage, cost, and latency using a model-free statistical (extractive) filter — no external models, services, or new dependencies. It rewrites `messages[].content` (for the configured roles) and the legacy top-level `prompt` in admitted OpenAI Chat/Text Completions bodies, replacing long content strings with shorter versions. The fixed families `responses` (OpenAI Responses `instructions` and `input` message text) and `anthropic_messages` (Anthropic `system` and `messages[].content` text blocks) are explicit opt-ins that `auto` never selects. The default `request_family: auto` requires the body shape to match a standard operation-path suffix (`/chat/completions` or `/completions`); a fixed family explicitly opts a compatible custom endpoint into compression. Shape validation still applies, and malformed JSON, provider-native, or ambiguous bodies that fail coarse family classification pass through unchanged. Valid JSON whose coarse shape is admitted (for example a `messages` array) but whose inner `role`/`content` fields are malformed skips statistical compression; with `preserve_tag` configured, that fallback can still perform marker-only cleanup of JSON string values, while without a configured marker it passes through unchanged.

Request buffering is only enabled for matching JSON `POST` requests without a non-`identity` `Content-Encoding`; with `preserve_tag` configured, encoded candidates are buffered too so the final hook can verify their decoded view.

Runs after `compression` request decompression.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `compress_roles` | String[] | `["user"]` | Message roles whose `content` is compressed (trimmed and case-insensitive; 1–32 entries of at most 64 characters, none blank). When it includes `user`, the legacy top-level `prompt` (and a string Responses `input`) is compressed too. |
| `target_ratio` | Number | `0.5` | Fraction of word-tokens to keep. `0.5` ≈ 50% reduction; `0.3` is more aggressive. Strictly between 0 and 1. |
| `min_content_tokens` | Integer | `200` | Estimated-token floor per content string, from `0` through `131072`; shorter content is passed through unchanged. |
| `max_scan_bytes` | Integer | `1048576` | From `1` through `1048576` bytes. Skip statistical compression when the request body exceeds this size; configured marker sanitation remains active through the hard 1 MiB body/output bound. |
| `preserve_tag` | String | _(unset)_ | Optional marker name; text in `<TAG>…</TAG>` string values is kept verbatim and the markers are stripped. Object member names are never sanitized. Name must be 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_`. |
| `request_family` | String | `"auto"` | `auto`, `chat_completions`, `text_completions`, `responses`, or `anthropic_messages`. Fixed families opt compatible custom endpoint paths into compression; fixed `text_completions` requires `user` in `compress_roles` after trimming and case normalization. |
| `target_max_tokens` | Integer | _(unset)_ | Optional aggregate estimated-token budget (`1`–`131072`); requests within it are not compressed and larger ones lose only what is needed, never more than `target_ratio` allows. Best effort. |
| `mode` | String | `"enforce"` | `enforce` or `observe` (record `ai_prompt_compressor.observed_*` savings and forward the original prompt; markers are still removed). |
| `sample_rate` | Number | `1` | Fraction of requests (greater than 0, at most 1) eligible for statistical work; deterministic per request. |

The filter scores each word by stop-word membership, length, in-document rarity, and a proper-noun signal, then drops the lowest-scoring words until `target_ratio` is met. Fenced code blocks, inline code, URLs, numbers, `snake_case`/identifier tokens, and uppercase acronyms are always preserved, and negations (`not`, `NEVER`, `don’t`, …) and `unless`/`except`/`only` are kept with the word after them, along with conditions (`if`, `must`, `before`, `after`, `until`, `exactly`), quantifiers (`all`, `every`, `each`, `any`), and spelled-out numbers. Token counts are estimated (~4 characters per token); no model tokenizer is embedded.

Runs after `compression` so opt-in request decompression exposes plaintext prompt JSON before this plugin rewrites the authoritative request body. Its per-request gate buffers candidate JSON `POST` bodies; `before_proxy` rewrites `ctx.metadata["request_body"]` for already-plaintext compatibility and stores bounded private stage state; `transform_request_body_with_context` owns the authoritative upstream bytes and counters; and `on_final_request_body_with_context` rejects an unsanitizable decoded marker-bearing surface before dispatch — including (`400`) an admitted final body, or a content-coded body's decoded view, that still carries a configured marker in a string value. `ai_federation` consumes that final body after the transform, so plaintext and opt-in compressed uploads use the same governed representation. Under `auto`, only `messages[].content` and the legacy `prompt` are compressed, and embeddings `input` and Anthropic top-level `system` are left intact; Responses `instructions`/`input` and the Anthropic `system` prompt are compressed only under the `responses` / `anthropic_messages` fixed families. When a field is statistically rewritten, it records `ai_prompt_compressor.original_tokens`, `.compressed_tokens`, `.tokens_saved`, and `.fields_compressed` metadata for logging (`.observed_*` in observe mode), and a skipped compression records `ai_prompt_compressor.instances.<id>.skipped` (`saturated`, `work_limit`, or `not_sampled`). See [`ai_prompt_compressor.md`](ai_prompt_compressor.md) for the full reference.

When bounded work or output limits select the representation-preserving marker
fallback, sanitation is value-only: configured markers are removed from JSON
string values, while every object member name remains byte-for-byte unchanged,
including escaped spellings, duplicate members, nesting, and surrounding
whitespace. Invalid or truncated JSON is not admitted and is left untouched.

```yaml
plugin_name: ai_prompt_compressor
config:
  compress_roles: [user, system]
  target_ratio: 0.4
  min_content_tokens: 150
  preserve_tag: keep
```

### `ai_response_guard`

**Priority:** 4075 · **Phases:** `after_proxy`, `on_response_body`, `transform_response_body`, `finalize_client_visible_response_body` · **Protocols:** HTTP, gRPC · **Failure policy:** `FailClosed`

Validates and filters LLM response content before it reaches the client. Complements `ai_prompt_shield` (which guards inputs) by providing output-side guardrails including PII detection in responses, keyword/phrase blocklists, and response format validation. Native gRPC responses are supported through an explicit, descriptor-based `grpc` enrollment block (see **Native gRPC inspection** below); methods that are not enrolled are never decoded, never inspected, and never forced onto the buffered path.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | String | `"reject"` | `reject` (502), `redact`, or `warn` |
| `pii_patterns` | String[] | `[]` | Built-in PII patterns to scan for in responses; each name at most once |
| `custom_pii_patterns` | Object[] | `[]` | Custom `{name, regex}` PII patterns, at most 256 entries. `regex` must not match the empty string; `name` is at most 128 characters |
| `blocked_phrases` | String[] | `[]` | Case-insensitive literal phrases to block, at most 1024 entries |
| `blocked_patterns` | Object[] | `[]` | Custom `{name, regex}` content patterns to block, at most 256 entries. `regex` must not match the empty string; `name` is at most 128 characters |
| `scan_fields` | String | `"content"` | `content` (supported completion and tool/function-call fields) or `all` (entire body) |
| `redaction_placeholder` | String | `"[REDACTED:{type}]"` | Template for redacted text; the rendered result is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes |
| `max_scan_bytes` | Integer | `1048576` | Maximum governed buffered body size (hard ceiling `67108864`, 64 MiB), including buffered non-2xx error bodies and the aggregate decoded/decompressed native-gRPC payload across frames; reject/redact and structural rules fail closed above it, while warn-only content rules record a bounded warning and pass through |
| `require_json` | bool | `false` | Reject responses that are not valid JSON |
| `required_fields` | String[] | `[]` | Required top-level JSON fields (rejects with 502 if missing) |
| `max_completion_length` | Integer | `0` | Maximum completion text length in characters — Unicode scalar values, not UTF-8 bytes (0 = unlimited) |
| `allowlist` | Object | — | PII exceptions (see **Allowlist** below): `values` (exact matched strings, at most 1024, each 1–1024 bytes) and `patterns` (regexes that must match the whole matched text, at most 256) |
| `grpc` | Object | — | Native-gRPC inspection contract (see below). Absent means the plugin stays HTTP-only |

At least one non-empty `pii_patterns`, `custom_pii_patterns`, `blocked_phrases`, `blocked_patterns`, or `required_fields` list, `require_json: true`, or positive `max_completion_length` must be configured.

**Native gRPC inspection.** Set `grpc` to enroll specific methods for schema-aware protobuf response inspection. The block is closed (`descriptor_path`, `methods`, `max_message_bytes`, `max_messages`); each `methods` entry is closed too (`response_type`, `text_fields`).

| `grpc` field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `descriptor_path` | String | — | **Required.** Node-local path to a compiled `FileDescriptorSet` (`protoc --descriptor_set_out`) |
| `methods` | Object | — | **Required, non-empty.** Map of `/package.Service/Method` → method contract. Only these methods are inspected. Every dotted service segment and the method identifier must be a protobuf/gRPC identifier; an optional leading slash is normalized and duplicates after normalization are rejected |
| `methods.<path>.response_type` | String | — | **Required.** Fully-qualified response message type, resolved in the descriptor pool at construction |
| `methods.<path>.text_fields` | String[] | all string fields | Non-empty list of dotted field paths (e.g. `reply.text`), each with 1–32 segments that remain non-empty after trimming whitespace. Paths must be unique after segment trimming, end at a `string` field, and may traverse repeated messages but not `map` fields. Omit to inspect every string field recursively |
| `max_message_bytes` | Integer | `1048576` | Per-message ceiling, applied to the declared frame length and enforced while inflating a compressed frame — inflation stops at the tighter of this ceiling and the remaining `max_scan_bytes` budget. Aggregate decoded/decompressed payload across frames is additionally capped by `max_scan_bytes` |
| `max_messages` | Integer | `64` | Maximum length-prefixed frames in one buffered response |

Semantics:

- **Enrollment is the whole scope.** A gRPC response whose method is not in `methods` is not inspected and does not vote for response-body buffering, so unrelated gRPC traffic keeps streaming. The method comes from `grpc_full_method` (published by `grpc_method_router`, so a method rewrite is honored), otherwise from the backend-effective path the proxy binds at the backend-path boundary — a `grpc`-enrolled guard joins that boundary itself, so `strip_listen_path`, a proxy `backend_path`, or a target path is resolved to the method the backend actually serves without a companion `grpc_method_router` — and only for a reply produced before dispatch (a mock, for example) from the client request path.
- **Framing and compression.** The buffered body is parsed as complete length-prefixed frames; a truncated frame, a stray trailing byte, or an unrecognized compressed-flag value is malformed. A compressed frame is inflated only when `grpc-encoding` is `gzip`, and the compressed payload must be exactly one fully consumed gzip member (trailing garbage and concatenated members are rejected). Any other encoding is uninspectable. Redaction re-frames the response and re-compresses the frames that arrived compressed, so `grpc-encoding` stays truthful.
- **Trailers.** Unchanged responses preserve trailers. When redaction rewrites the body, the shared body-rewrite policy retains reserved gRPC terminal metadata (`grpc-status`, `grpc-message`, and `grpc-status-details-bin`) and retires application trailers and their merged-header copies.
- **Streaming.** Server-streaming responses are inspected as their concatenated frames, bounded by `max_messages`, per-message `max_message_bytes`, and an aggregate decoded/decompressed ceiling of `max_scan_bytes`; nothing is buffered without a bound, and exceeding any bound is uninspectable rather than partially inspected. Selected string fields are scanned both individually and as an ordered aggregate so a blocked phrase or length overflow split across frames cannot bypass the guard; redact mode fails closed when a match exists only across string/frame boundaries.
- **Redaction is verified, not assumed.** `action: redact` rewrites the selected string fields (including known protobuf extensions when `text_fields` is omitted), re-encodes, then re-parses and re-scans the exact bytes the client would receive with the same selected-field and aggregate semantics. Like the HTTP verifier, the re-scan ignores this instance's own rendered placeholders (a `blocked_patterns` rule whose name matches its own regex still redacts), and the final client-visible phase recognizes this instance's exact verified output under its `grpc-encoding`. Anything that does not come back clean — a protobuf map key (which, like a JSON object member name, cannot be rewritten), a cross-boundary-only match, a rewrite that does not survive the round trip, or a gRPC-Web translated response whose body is re-framed by `grpc_web` before this transform could run — is rejected with a gRPC error instead of being reported as redacted.
- **Fail-closed cases.** For `reject` and `redact`, all of these produce a gRPC error: a descriptor that cannot be read on this node, a payload that does not decode as the configured type, unknown fields retained on the decoded protobuf message tree (their bytes are not inspectable, so a clean scan of known fields is not evidence), a body or aggregate decoded payload above `max_scan_bytes`, exceeding the walk depth/node budgets, and every framing/compression case above. The guard inspects decoded messages, not original wire bytes: an extra field inside a known map-entry wire message can be discarded by protobuf decoding before the unknown-field walk and is not rejected by this unknown-field check. `action: warn` records the same reasons in `ai_response_guard_warning` and passes the response through.
- **Not covered.** `bytes` fields are opaque and are not scanned. With `grpc`, `require_json` must be omitted or `false`, and `required_fields` must be omitted or empty: active JSON structural rules cannot describe protobuf messages. At least one detection pattern, blocked phrase, or positive `max_completion_length` is required. Request-side protobuf inspection is `body_validator`'s job.
- **Framing outside the contract.** A gRPC-framed response on a request that is *not* native gRPC has no enrolled method naming its message type, and the protobuf rewrite path declines it. Its length-prefixed frames are not a JSON/SSE/text document either, so `scan_fields: all` must not scan them as raw text and promise a redaction that can never be applied: enforcing actions reject and `warn` records `grpc_framed_response_requires_grpc_contract`, matching what content mode already did for the same response. This covers gRPC-Web as well as `application/grpc` — a browser gRPC-Web request is `HttpFlavor::Plain`, and `grpc_web` relabels every translated response to `application/grpc-web*` before this plugin inspects it, so the framing is resolved from the live media type, the pristine backend media type stamped before any response hook ran, and finally a total frame parse under the grammar the client's representation admits. A genuine bare JSON document on a gRPC-Web request is still inspected normally.
- **Reject shape.** A plugin reject on an `application/grpc` response is normalized by the proxy into a trailers-only gRPC error, so clients see a gRPC status rather than an HTTP JSON body.
- **Config admission.** The `grpc` block is validated shape-only at Admin/CP admission (no data-plane descriptor file required) and against the real `FileDescriptorSet` by mode-aware file-dependency validation: fatal in file mode, warn in DB mode. The OpenAPI schema checks selector segment syntax, the 32-segment bound, and exact duplicates; uniqueness after segment trimming and descriptor field resolution still require runtime validation. On a DP, a readable but invalid descriptor rejects the candidate configuration and retains the last-known-good generation; an absent or unreadable descriptor keeps the enrollment set so enrolled methods fail closed at request time rather than rejecting the DP update.

**Built-in PII patterns** (same as `ai_prompt_shield`): `ssn`, `credit_card`, `email`, `phone_us`, `api_key`, `aws_key`, `ip_address`, `iban`

The shared catalog (`plugins/utils/ai_pii.rs`) covers:

- `credit_card` — 16–19 digit Visa, Mastercard (`51`–`55` and the `2221`–`2720` 2-series), Discover, UnionPay (`62`), and JCB (`3528`–`3589`) numbers in 4-digit groups; 15-digit American Express contiguous, in its printed 4-6-5 grouping (`3782 822463 10005`), or as 4-4-4-3; and 14-digit Diners Club contiguous or 4-6-4. Groups may be separated by `-`, `.`, or whitespace. This guard (and `ai_transcript_audit`) confirms every candidate with a **Luhn checksum**, so a card-shaped order or tracking number that fails the checksum is neither reported, rejected, nor redacted. A separate 1–3 digit token directly after a complete card (`4111 1111 1111 1111 123`, a card and its security code) joins the match; the card is still confirmed and the whole span, code included, is redacted.
- `api_key` — a `sk`/`pk`/`rk`/`api`/`key`/`token`/`secret`/`password` prefix, up to three short `-`/`_` segments (`sk-proj-…`, `sk-ant-api03-…`, `sk-svcacct-…`), a run of at least 20 alphanumerics, and every further `-`/`_` segment of the same token (consecutive separators and trailing underscores included), so redaction removes the whole credential; plus GitHub (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_`, `github_pat_`), Google (`AIza…`, matched in full even when its 39th character is `-`), and Slack (`xox[abposr]-…`) token formats.
- `ip_address` — IPv4 dotted quads with every octet `0`–`255`, and IPv6 in full eight-group form or `::`-compressed (inner, or trailing as in `2001:db8:1234::`) with at least three groups. A bare `::`, leading-`::` forms such as `::1`, and two-group compressions such as `fe80::1` are not matched because they are indistinguishable from `Type::member` paths in code; the IPv4 part of `::ffff:192.0.2.1` is still matched.
- `iban` — an IBAN-registry country code, two check digits, and an 11–30 character BBAN, compact or in the printed space-separated groups of four (`GB29 NWBK 6016 1331 9268 19`).

**Allowlist.** `allowlist.values` lists exact strings and `allowlist.patterns` lists regexes (each anchored to match the whole text, `^(?:…)$`) that are never PII findings — for example a vendor's public `support@…` address or an order-number family that happens to look like a card. An exception is compared against the COMPLETE text a `pii_patterns` / `custom_pii_patterns` regex matched, so an allowed value embedded in a longer match does not excuse it, and a non-allowed sibling value in the same response is still detected. It applies identically to detection, redaction (an allowed match is left verbatim), and the residual re-scans, in every action. `blocked_phrases` and `blocked_patterns` are never excused. The block is closed (`values`, `patterns`); each pattern must compile on its own.

Unknown built-in pattern names and built-in patterns that fail to compile are fatal at construction time. All configured patterns are merged into a single `RegexSet` for O(text_len) detection per scan.

In `scan_fields: "all"` mode, the recursive redactor preserves only **top-level scalar** structural fields (`id`, `model`, `created`, `role`, `type`, `index`, `finish_reason`, `usage`, etc.) so timestamps and identifiers that look like dotted-quad IPs or other PII patterns are not corrupted. It always recurses into nested objects and arrays — including nested occurrences of those same key names — so PII cannot evade redaction by being nested under a structural key (e.g. `{"choices":[{"message":{"type":"<SSN>"}}]}` is still redacted). This recursive behavior applies across the full decoded JSON tree; `scan_fields: "content"` alone limits rewriting to supported completion fields.

The `redaction_placeholder` template is emitted literally: any `$`-sequences in it or in an operator-supplied custom pattern name are written verbatim and are never interpreted as regex capture-group references. Literal blocked phrases never become public identifiers: placeholders, reject bodies, metadata, and logs use bounded positional IDs such as `blocked_phrase:0`, never the configured phrase itself.

**Bounded redaction output.** The same controls as `ai_prompt_shield` apply. A `custom_pii_patterns` or `blocked_patterns` regex that matches the empty string is refused at construction, and a zero-width span produced at run time by a contextual assertion (for example a bare `\b`) makes redaction fail closed instead of inserting a placeholder at every position. Pattern names are capped at 128 characters and each rendered placeholder at 512 bytes. Whole-body text redaction is written through the response's retained-body ceiling; structured JSON, SSE, and gRPC redaction, which rewrites one string at a time, shares one growth allowance per response of four times the body size (64 KiB floor, 64 MiB ceiling), never more than the room the response's retained-body ceiling leaves above the body. Growth is measured on the JSON-escaped form, and live intermediate buffers are bounded by the same allowance, so a rewrite can be refused even when its final net growth would fit. A refused SSE rewrite is never treated as a no-op. Sequential patterns that keep rewriting each other's placeholders exhaust that allowance and the response fails closed (502) rather than delivering a partially redacted body.

**Streaming (SSE):** Request-controlled `Accept: text/event-stream` and internal streaming markers never waive the guard. An active guard buffers conservatively until the pristine backend representation is known. A genuine backend `text/event-stream` response is decided before header commit: `reject`, `redact`, and structural enforcement reject with HTTP 502 because complete inspection of an unbounded stream cannot be promised; a genuinely warn-only guard records the uninspectable response and permits it. A later response-header plugin cannot manufacture or erase the pristine content type used for this decision, and a missing or ambiguous backend type remains on the ordinary buffered inspection path. The existing bounded SSE parser remains applicable to finite gateway-generated or otherwise already-buffered SSE bodies: it joins legal multi-`data:` events, accepts LF, CRLF, or lone-CR line ends in any mix after ignoring leading UTF-8 BOMs (inspection and redaction split lines identically, so such streams are redacted rather than refused), preserves each line's original terminator and any leading BOMs when rewriting (except that an LF-terminated blank line directly after a line ending in a lone CR is written as CRLF, so the pair cannot merge into one line end and swallow the blank line that dispatches the event), and fails closed for enforcing/redacting malformed or non-UTF-8 content.

**Multi-provider support:** Content mode covers OpenAI chat text strings and content-part arrays (including `{type: refusal}` parts and message/delta `refusal` strings), tool/function names and arguments, legacy `choices[].text`/`function_call`, Responses API `output_text` and `output[].{content,arguments}`, Anthropic `content[].text` plus a tool block's `content[].name` and `content[].input` and an extended-thinking block's `content[].thinking`, chat-dialect reasoning (`choices[].message` / `delta` `reasoning_content` and `reasoning` strings, buffered and streamed), Responses API reasoning `output[].summary[].text` (and streamed `reasoning_summary_text` / `reasoning_text` deltas), Google Gemini `candidates[].content.parts[].text` plus `functionCall` names and arguments (buffered as well as streamed), and Amazon Bedrock Converse `output.message.content[].text` plus a `toolUse` block's `name` and decoded `input` and a `reasoningContent` block's `reasoningText.text` (an object `output`, distinct from the Responses API `output` array, whose blocks carry no `type` discriminator). Redacting an Anthropic `thinking` or Converse reasoning block invalidates that block's provider `signature`, so a client that replays it in a later turn will be refused by the provider; `reject` does not have this effect. Four provider shapes that are not an OpenAI-style object are covered as well: Cohere v1 `/chat` and `/generate` (`text`, plus the echoed `chat_history[].message` turns — this plugin has no `exclude_roles` knob, so every echoed turn is scanned whatever case its `role` is spelled in), Amazon Bedrock Titan (`results[].outputText`), Ollama `/api/generate` (the top-level `response` string), and Hugging Face TGI, whose completion document is a top-level JSON **array** of `{"generated_text": …}` objects with no object root at all. Adjacent text-bearing parts of one content array (and adjacent Anthropic text blocks / Gemini parts) are joined before detection and length enforcement, so a match or length overflow split across part boundaries cannot bypass the guard; a redact-mode match that exists only across part boundaries fails closed with 502. Tool/function `arguments` are nested JSON serialized into a string: both modes scan the raw string and its decoded tokens (one bounded parse per argument string), and redact mode rewrites the decoded document — argument content that cannot be rewritten (a decoded object key or numeric scalar) fails closed. A tool document that arrives already decoded rather than as a serialized string — an Anthropic `tool_use` block's `input`, a Gemini `functionCall`'s `args` — contributes its decoded tokens the same way and is redacted value-safely under the same rule. Every one of these extractions is one level deep: a block or result contributes its own fields and nothing recurses back into the response envelope. A tool block's `name` / `input` are read untyped, exactly as `ai_semantic_firewall`'s `$.content[*].name` / `$.content[*].input` are, so `tool_use`, `server_tool_use`, and `mcp_tool_use` blocks are all covered. Two of these arms are broad by construction on a shared proxy: any response with a top-level `response` string (Ollama), and any array `content` whose elements carry `name` / `input`, contribute content-mode text. Scope the plugin to AI routes if a mixed proxy must keep such business bodies outside the guard. The buffered SSE path reassembles the corresponding OpenAI chat/tool, Responses API, and refusal deltas before detection and applies the same decoded-argument scanning. Google Gemini `streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` streams are reassembled by the same shared reassembler — a candidate's incremental `parts[].text` fragments concatenated per candidate `index`, plus that candidate's `functionCall` name and compactly serialized `args` document, whose decoded tokens are scanned like any other tool arguments — so a match split across frames or across a candidate's parts is caught. A Gemini stream carrying a part kind the reassembler cannot fold (`inlineData`, `fileData`, `executableCode`, `codeExecutionResult`, a `thought` summary), a frame that claims the shape while violating it (a non-array `candidates`, a non-array `content.parts`, a non-string `text`, a malformed `functionCall`), or a candidate index at or beyond the 64-candidate ceiling is reported as `uninspectable_sse` and fails closed for enforcing actions. Anthropic Messages event streams are reassembled the same way — `content_block_delta` `text_delta` prose and `input_json_delta` tool input concatenated per content-block `index`, plus the `content_block_start` tool name and non-empty `input` object, a populated `message_start` `message.content` envelope, and an `error` event's `error.message` — dispatched from the SSE `event:` line, the JSON `type` field, or both, and the decoded-argument scan covers the reassembled tool input. An Anthropic stream carrying an event, a `delta.type`, or a block index the reassembler cannot cover (extended thinking's `thinking_delta`, an interleaved foreign frame, or an index at or beyond the 64-block ceiling) is reported as `uninspectable_sse` the same way and fails closed for enforcing actions rather than being cleared on the prose that did reassemble. Hugging Face TGI `/generate_stream` streams are reassembled by the same shared reassembler — the per-frame `token.text` fragments concatenated into the buffered document's `$[*].generated_text`, with the terminal frame's completed `generated_text` skipped when the accumulated text already ends with it (so the completion is never scanned twice) and appended when it diverges from the deltas. Frames are selected structurally (a `token` object or a string `generated_text`, with none of the other protocols' discriminators beside them) so an unrelated event stream carrying a `token` field is never claimed, and stickily thereafter so a stream already identified as TGI cannot hide a fragment by mistyping the field. A TGI stream carrying a frame that violates the protocol (a `token` that is not an object with a string `text`, a `generated_text` that is neither a string nor `null`), or carrying model text outside the reconstructed completion (a non-empty `top_tokens` alternatives array, a `details.best_of_sequences` list), is reported as `uninspectable_sse` and fails closed for enforcing actions. Cohere v1 streaming is **not SSE at all** — it is newline-delimited JSON under `application/stream+json` (`event_type` of `stream-start` / `text-generation` / `stream-end`) — so no SSE path applies to it; such a body reaches the buffered JSON path, where the concatenated objects are not one JSON document and enforcing actions fail closed as `invalid_json` (a single-object stream that happens to parse is read through the ordinary buffered arms). Cohere v2 `/v2/chat` is ordinary SSE. A genuine backend `text/event-stream` response is rejected before header commit for every enforcing action regardless, so the SSE path affects only finite gateway-generated or already-buffered SSE bodies. Detection and redaction cover the same buffered field set — every field the Content-mode detector walks, `action: redact` rewrites.

**What `redact` rewrites in a TGI stream.** A frame's `token.text` fragment and the terminal `generated_text`. Both are plain strings, so both are rewritten directly. A match that exists only ACROSS frames — a card number split between two token fragments — is not rewritable in any single frame; the post-redaction re-scan reassembles the stream, still sees it, and the response is rejected with HTTP 502 rather than delivered.

**What `redact` rewrites in a Gemini stream.** `candidates[].content.parts[].text` prose, `candidates[].content.parts[].functionCall.name`, and `candidates[].content.parts[].functionCall.args`. `args` arrives as a JSON object rather than the serialized string OpenAI and Anthropic use, so it gets the same value-safe treatment as a decoded tool-argument document: string values are rewritten, while object member names and non-string scalars are left alone and a match confined to one of those fails closed through the post-redaction re-scan instead of being rewritten into an invalid document. A match that exists only ACROSS frames — a card number split between two frames of one candidate — is likewise not rewritable in any single frame; the re-scan reassembles the stream, still sees it, and the response is rejected with HTTP 502 rather than delivered.

**What `redact` rewrites in an Anthropic stream.** `content_block_delta.delta.text` prose, `content_block_delta.delta.partial_json` tool-input fragments (under the same rule as OpenAI tool-call `arguments`: value-safe redaction of the decoded document when the fragment is self-contained JSON, plain string redaction otherwise), `content_block_start.content_block.name`, and `error.error.message`. Frames are routed by the JSON `type` field when it is present and by the SSE `event:` line otherwise, so a stream stripped of the duplicated `type` is still rewritten. A match that exists only ACROSS fragments — an SSN split between two `input_json_delta` fragments, say — is not rewritable in any single frame; the post-redaction re-scan reassembles the stream, still sees it, and the response is rejected with HTTP 502 rather than delivered.

Unknown root fields and unknown keys inside custom pattern objects are rejected at construction. Enforcing actions also fail closed when a governed response is oversized, malformed, non-UTF-8, or not representable in content mode.

**Duplicate JSON members.** `serde_json` keeps the last of duplicate object members while a client's parser may keep the first, and the original bytes — every member included — are what the client receives. An overwritten member whose PII is `\u`-escaped is therefore invisible to both the decoded passes and the raw-body pass. When any detection, `required_fields`, or `max_completion_length` rule is active, a governed JSON response, a finite SSE `data:` payload, or a serialized tool `arguments` document (buffered, or reassembled across SSE frames) with duplicate member names — compared after escape decoding — is uninspectable: `reject` / `redact` (and structural rules) answer 502 with reason `ambiguous_json_document`, while `warn` records it in `ai_response_guard_warning` and continues. `require_json` alone is not affected, since duplicates do not change whether the body parses.

**Empty successful responses.** With `require_json` or `required_fields` active, an empty successful (2xx) body is refused (`empty_response_body`). This includes a zero-byte synthetic success — a `response_mock` or function reply — which the guard opts into the body pipeline for; HEAD and 1xx/204/205/304 keep their no-body semantics, and a guard with only content rules still accepts an empty body. `scan_fields: all` can inspect and redact arbitrary UTF-8 response text; `warn` remains explicitly non-enforcing and records a bounded warning for uninspectable content. When redaction changes body bytes, representation validators (`ETag`, `Last-Modified`, `Content-Digest`, `Repr-Digest`, `Digest`, and `Content-MD5`) are removed case-insensitively; clean responses retain them.

**Whole-body text redaction (`action: redact`).** Plain-text and other whole-body redaction paths apply configured patterns **sequentially** inside one ceiling-sized transform window. Each pass writes into a bounded sink while the prior pass buffer may still be resident; the shared ceiling budgets that scratch by **allocator capacity**, not logical length. With several patterns configured, geometric growth slack can therefore reduce the largest body that can be redacted to well below the per-response retained ceiling — often on the order of half that ceiling or less, depending on pattern count and allocator behavior — and the guard fails closed with `502` rather than forwarding partially redacted bytes. This is an operational limit of the fail-closed construction, not a separate tunable threshold.

**Final HTTP verification.** Origin-coded responses claimed by an enforcing rule reach the shared bounded decoder before final plaintext inspection; warn-only rules preserve the encoded response. Final verification recognizes this instance's exact residual-verified output, so its generated placeholders and preserved structural scalars do not become new violations. Later changes to the body or media type require fresh detection. Size, JSON structure, and completion-length checks still apply to the delivered output, and an unfulfilled redaction remains a rejection. When the delivered representation is byte-for-byte the one phase 9 already inspected and decided (same status, media type, and `grpc-encoding`, nothing deferred, no redaction pending), the final phase reuses that decision instead of parsing and scanning the body a second time; any change gets the full fresh pass.

**Scope.** Content rules (patterns, phrases, `required_fields`, `require_json`, `max_completion_length`) govern successful (2xx) responses only: under `reject` / `warn` a provider 4xx/5xx error body is not scanned, although `max_scan_bytes` applies to every buffered status and a `redact` transform may still rewrite a buffered error body it can parse. `warn` never adds a response header; its findings are visible only in the metadata below.

**Metadata keys** (for observability). Every key is a comma-separated list, and each write is a de-duplicated UNION with what is already there, so several guard instances on one proxy (say one redacting `email`, one warning on `ssn`) all keep their findings in transaction logs and `ai_transcript_audit` records:
- `ai_response_guard_detected` — detected pattern types (warn mode)
- `ai_response_guard_redacted` — redacted pattern types (redact mode)
- `ai_response_guard_rejected` — why a response was rejected: the detected pattern types, a fixed uninspectable reason code (below), `missing_required_field:<field>`, or a completion-length message
- `ai_response_guard_warning` — warn-mode completion-length messages and uninspectable reason codes: `body_exceeds_max_scan_bytes`, `empty_response_body`, `invalid_json`, `ambiguous_json_document`, `non_utf8_response`, `unsupported_response_content_type`, `uninspectable_sse`, `sse_cannot_satisfy_json_structure`, `streaming_response_requires_bounded_inspection`, `grpc_framed_response_requires_grpc_contract`, `encoded_response_not_decoded`, `grpc_web_translation_blocks_redaction`, and the `grpc_*` framing/descriptor/decode reasons

```yaml
plugin_name: ai_response_guard
config:
  action: redact
  pii_patterns: [ssn, credit_card, email, api_key]
  blocked_phrases: ["ignore all previous instructions"]
  blocked_patterns:
    - name: profanity
      regex: "\\b(?:badword1|badword2)\\b"
  max_completion_length: 10000
```

Native gRPC example:

```yaml
plugin_name: ai_response_guard
config:
  action: redact
  pii_patterns: [ssn, email]
  grpc:
    descriptor_path: /etc/ferrum/descriptors/assistant.bin
    max_messages: 32
    methods:
      "/assistant.Chat/Complete":
        response_type: assistant.CompleteResponse
        text_fields: ["reply.text"]
```

### AI Plugin Composition Example

A typical AI gateway proxy combining the AI plugins with `ai_federation` for multi-provider routing:

```yaml
# Proxy config. ai_federation answers only eligible requests (POST with a JSON
# content type); every other request that earlier plugins admit continues to
# ordinary backend dispatch. allowed_methods refuses non-POST methods with 405,
# but a non-JSON POST still reaches backend_host, so point it at a deliberate
# fallback service (for example one that answers 415/400), not a placeholder.
listen_path: /v1/chat/completions
allowed_methods: [POST]
backend_scheme: https
backend_host: ai-fallback.internal
backend_port: 443

# Plugins attached to this proxy, shown as plugin_name + config. In file mode each
# entry is a `plugin_configs` item referenced from the proxy's `plugins` list.
# They run in priority order regardless of list order.
plugins:
  - plugin_name: key_auth
    config: {}
  - plugin_name: ai_prompt_shield
    config:
      action: redact
      patterns: [ssn, credit_card, email, api_key]
  - plugin_name: ai_semantic_firewall
    config:
      provider:
        type: openai_compatible_embeddings
        endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/embeddings
        model: text-embedding-3-small
  - plugin_name: ai_request_guard
    config:
      allowed_models: [claude-sonnet-4-20250514, gpt-4o, gemini-2.0-flash]   # exact names, no globs
      max_tokens_limit: 4096
      enforce_max_tokens: clamp
      default_max_tokens: 1024
  - plugin_name: ai_semantic_cache
    config:
      ttl_seconds: 600
      include_model_in_key: true
      scope_by_consumer: true
  - plugin_name: ai_federation
    config:
      providers:
        - name: anthropic
          provider_type: anthropic
          api_key: "sk-ant-..."
          priority: 1
          model_patterns: ["claude-*"]
        - name: openai
          provider_type: openai
          api_key: "sk-..."
          priority: 2
          model_patterns: ["gpt-*"]
        - name: gemini
          provider_type: google_gemini
          api_key: "AIza..."
          priority: 3
          model_patterns: ["gemini-*"]
      fallback_enabled: true
      fail_on_missing_model: true
      fail_on_no_matching_provider: true
  - plugin_name: ai_response_guard
    config:
      action: redact
      pii_patterns: [ssn, credit_card, email]
      blocked_phrases: ["ignore all previous instructions"]
  - plugin_name: ai_rate_limiter
    config:
      token_limit: 1000000
      window_seconds: 86400
      limit_by: consumer
      expose_headers: true
  - plugin_name: stdout_logging
    config: {}
```

> **Note:** `ai_federation` short-circuits normal backend dispatch via `RejectBinary` for the requests it handles, but successful buffered synthetic bodies still run through response-body hooks: `ai_response_guard` inspects/transforms the normalized provider body, and `ai_semantic_cache` (4057, ahead of federation) answers repeats from cache and stores a provider-backed 2xx federation answer on a miss, so the pairing populates the cache. `ai_token_metrics` is the deliberate exception and does not inspect federation's synthetic response; federation writes the same token metadata keys directly. Separately, `ai_rate_limiter` records federation token usage through `applies_after_proxy_on_reject` on the rejection path.

> **Limitation — `on_unmetered_response: "reject"` cannot replace a federated response.** Federation dispatches from the final request-body phase, so `ai_rate_limiter` performs its normal pre-reservation before provider I/O. The response still travels through the synthetic rejection pipeline, whose reconciliation hook cannot replace an already selected response. `charge_estimate` and `warn` therefore reconcile correctly, but `reject` records the violation without substituting a 502. If fail-closed unmetered responses are required, require provider usage during federation normalization or enforce it upstream.

## MCP / Agent Tool Gateway Plugin

### `mcp_gateway`

**Priority:** 2992 · **Phases:** `before_proxy`, `transform_request_body`, `enforce_final_backend_header_policy`, `on_final_request_body`, `normalize_response_body`, `transform_response_body`, `after_proxy`, `on_final_response_body` · **Protocols:** HTTP · **Failure policy:** `FailClosed`

HTTP-only Model Context Protocol gateway for AI agent tool traffic. `transparent_proxy` mode routes one Ferrum endpoint to one upstream MCP server while preserving MCP JSON-RPC and session headers. `aggregate_router` mode exposes one endpoint for several upstream MCP servers: it aggregates and namespaces their tools, resources, and prompts, routes calls back to the owning upstream, validates tool arguments, applies per-tool policy, and emits `mcp.*` metadata for authorization, logging, tracing, chargeback, and alert plugins.

```yaml
      namespace: tools
```
